subject: medicine
title: What does a doctor actually spend the day doing?
question: What do you think a doctor actually spends most of their day doing?
answer: Discussion question — no single verdict. A strong foundation-level answer names something mundane and realistic (documentation, communication, coordination with a team, managing uncertainty) rather than a cure-focused, TV-drama account of constant dramatic intervention.
modelReasoningPath: A gentle realism check and a good early-confidence-builder — most of the day-to-day is management, communication and coordination rather than dramatic moments, and a candidate who can name even one concrete, mundane element (writing up notes, discussing a case with the team, explaining something to a worried patient) already shows more insight than a purely television-informed answer. This is not meant to be a hard station; it's an accessible way into realism about the job.

rubric.strong: Names at least one concrete, mundane element of the job realistically, and shows the doctor's contribution is about more than dramatic moments.
rubric.developing: Gives a reasonable answer but stays fairly general, without a specific concrete example.
rubric.weak: Gives a purely dramatic, cure-focused account with nothing mundane or realistic named at all.

commonMistakes.mistake: Cannot name anything mundane about the job
commonMistakes.reveals: Suggests their picture of medicine comes mainly from television or drama rather than real observation
A weak basis for understanding what the job actually involves day to day

liveProbes.probe: Where did that picture of the job come from?
liveProbes.goodResponse: Names real observation or work experience rather than television or assumption

hints: Think beyond the dramatic moments — what fills most of the actual hours?
Have you seen or read about this from a real source, or is it mostly an impression?
